study_title: RNA-seq of Fusarium graminearum under predation by the springtail Folsomia candida against untreated controls
experiment_title: NextSeq 500 paired end sequencing: RNA-seq of Fusarium graminearum under predation by the springtail Folsomia candida against untreated controls
sample_description: Protocols: Mycelium was harvested and springtails were removed. Whole mycelium was used to extract the RNA. 5,000 fungal spores in 5 µL water were inoculated onto three rice kernels autoclaved with 200 µl demineralized water in 15 ml Falcon tubes and incubated at 15°C in dark for 7-8 days 20 mg (around 200 individual animal) of springtail Folsomia candida starved for two days were placed into mycelia and the incubated at 15°C in dark. Controls were incubated under the same conditions without animals. Each group consisted of 4 replicates. Suspension of mycelia in 400 µl of RNA extraction solution [95% deionized formamide, 18 mM EDTA, 0.025% SDS, and 1% 2-mercaptoethanol] was disrupted by shaking with zirconia beads (2.0 mm diameter, Carl Roth, Karlsruhe, Germany) in reciprocal mill MM 200 (Retsch, Haan, Germany) for 2 min at maximum power, followed by incubation at 95°C for 7 min. Cells debris was removed by centrifugation at 16,000x g for 5 min at room temperature. The supernatant was transferred into RNA precipitation mixture consisting of 800 µl of isobutanol, 400 µl of 5 M guanidine thiocyanate and 5 µl of linear polyacrylamide used as co-precipitant (Co-Precipitant Pink, Bioline, London, UK). The mixture was centrifuged at 16,000x g for 5 min at room temperature and the pellet was washed with 75% ethanol, dried and dissolved in RNAase-free water. Strand-specific cDNA libraries were prepared using Illumina’s TruSeq stranded mRNA kit (75 bp paired-end).

study_title: Transcriptome-based comparison of the infection response in maize silks between Fusarium graminearum and Ustilago maydis
experiment_title: Illumina HiSeq 1000 paired end sequencing: Transcriptome-based comparison of the infection response in maize silks between Fusarium graminearum and Ustilago maydis
sample_description: Protocols: Fusarium conidia were grown and cultivated in Erlenmeyer flasks that contain liquid complete medium as 25-40% of the total volume of the flask for 3 days on a rotary shaker at 175 rpm, at 28°C. The mycelium was then separated from the medium by filtration, washed up and stored at -80°C. Total RNA was prepared by grinding tissues in liquid nitrogen and total RNA was extracted by TRIzol reagent (TRIzol Plus RNA Purification Kit, Ambion) and processed following the protocol provided by manufacturer. To remove DNA within extraction and purification procedures, total RNA was treated with DNase (Qiagen), then total RNA was quantified and visualized on a Bioanalyzer (Agilent). Library preparation and RNAseq were carried out as described in the Illumina TruSeq RNA Sample Preparation v2 Guide, the Illumina HiSeq 1000 System User Guide (Illumina, Inc., San Diego, CA, USA), and the KAPA Library Quantification Kit - Illumina/ABI Prism User Guide (Kapa Biosystems, Inc., Woburn, MA, USA). In brief, 500 ng of total RNA was used for purifying the poly-A containing mRNA molecules using poly-dT oligo-attached magnetic beads. Following purification, the mRNA was fragmented to an average insert size of 200-400 bases using divalent cations under elevated temperature (94°C for 4 minutes). The cleaved RNA fragments were copied into first strand cDNA using reverse transcriptase and random primers, followed by second strand cDNA synthesis using DNA Polymerase I and RNase H. The resulting cDNA fragments subsequently went through an end repair process, the addition of a single ‘A’ base, the ligation of the adapters, and a purification step. Finally the cDNA libraries were created by PCR enrichment. The libraries were quantified using the KAPA SYBR FAST ABI Prism Library Quantification Kit. Equimolar amounts of each library were used for cluster generation on the cBot (TruSeq PE Cluster Kit v3)

study_title: RNA-seq of Fusarium graminearum under predation by the springtail Folsomia candida against untreated controls
experiment_title: NextSeq 500 paired end sequencing: RNA-seq of Fusarium graminearum under predation by the springtail Folsomia candida against untreated controls
sample_description: Protocols: Mycelium was harvested and springtails were removed. Whole mycelium was used to extract the RNA. 5,000 fungal spores in 5 µL water were inoculated onto three rice kernels autoclaved with 200 µl demineralized water in 15 ml Falcon tubes and incubated at 15°C in dark for 7-8 days 20 mg (around 200 individual animal) of springtail Folsomia candida starved for two days were placed into mycelia and the incubated at 15°C in dark. Controls were incubated under the same conditions without animals. Each group consisted of 4 replicates. Suspension of mycelia in 400 µl of RNA extraction solution [95% deionized formamide, 18 mM EDTA, 0.025% SDS, and 1% 2-mercaptoethanol] was disrupted by shaking with zirconia beads (2.0 mm diameter, Carl Roth, Karlsruhe, Germany) in reciprocal mill MM 200 (Retsch, Haan, Germany) for 2 min at maximum power, followed by incubation at 95°C for 7 min. Cells debris was removed by centrifugation at 16,000x g for 5 min at room temperature. The supernatant was transferred into RNA precipitation mixture consisting of 800 µl of isobutanol, 400 µl of 5 M guanidine thiocyanate and 5 µl of linear polyacrylamide used as co-precipitant (Co-Precipitant Pink, Bioline, London, UK). The mixture was centrifuged at 16,000x g for 5 min at room temperature and the pellet was washed with 75% ethanol, dried and dissolved in RNAase-free water. Strand-specific cDNA libraries were prepared using Illumina’s TruSeq stranded mRNA kit (75 bp paired-end).

sample_title: RNAseq reads of Fusarium graminearum cultivated in Bacillus velezensis (EU07 strain) metabolites
sample_description: Bacillus species have prominent potential to suppress and compete with pathogenic microorganisms. In this study to elucidate the antagonistic mechanism, whole genome expression profiling of F. graminearum co-cultivated with EU07 culture filtrate was investigated in the presence and absence of culture filtrate of the bacterial strain. RNA-seq analysis obtained a comprehensive overview of the responsive pathogenic behaviour of F. graminearum classified according to biological and metabolic processes. We have determined all suppressed genes under biotic stress of EU07 on the pathogen. These findings delineate the functional inhibition of biosynthesis and corresponding pathways of F. graminearum by the antagonistic behaviour of EU07 and key insights targeting pathogen suppression.

study_title: RNA-seq of Fusarium graminearum under predation by the springtail Folsomia candida against untreated controls
experiment_title: NextSeq 500 paired end sequencing: RNA-seq of Fusarium graminearum under predation by the springtail Folsomia candida against untreated controls
sample_description: Protocols: Mycelium was harvested and springtails were removed. Whole mycelium was used to extract the RNA. 5,000 fungal spores in 5 µL water were inoculated onto three rice kernels autoclaved with 200 µl demineralized water in 15 ml Falcon tubes and incubated at 15°C in dark for 7-8 days 20 mg (around 200 individual animal) of springtail Folsomia candida starved for two days were placed into mycelia and the incubated at 15°C in dark. Controls were incubated under the same conditions without animals. Each group consisted of 4 replicates. Suspension of mycelia in 400 µl of RNA extraction solution [95% deionized formamide, 18 mM EDTA, 0.025% SDS, and 1% 2-mercaptoethanol] was disrupted by shaking with zirconia beads (2.0 mm diameter, Carl Roth, Karlsruhe, Germany) in reciprocal mill MM 200 (Retsch, Haan, Germany) for 2 min at maximum power, followed by incubation at 95°C for 7 min. Cells debris was removed by centrifugation at 16,000x g for 5 min at room temperature. The supernatant was transferred into RNA precipitation mixture consisting of 800 µl of isobutanol, 400 µl of 5 M guanidine thiocyanate and 5 µl of linear polyacrylamide used as co-precipitant (Co-Precipitant Pink, Bioline, London, UK). The mixture was centrifuged at 16,000x g for 5 min at room temperature and the pellet was washed with 75% ethanol, dried and dissolved in RNAase-free water. Strand-specific cDNA libraries were prepared using Illumina’s TruSeq stranded mRNA kit (75 bp paired-end).
description: NextSeq 500 paired end sequencing: RNA-seq of Fusarium graminearum under predation by the springtail Folsomia candida against untreated controls

study_title: Transcriptome-based comparison of the infection response in maize silks between Fusarium graminearum and Ustilago maydis
experiment_title: Illumina HiSeq 1000 paired end sequencing: Transcriptome-based comparison of the infection response in maize silks between Fusarium graminearum and Ustilago maydis
sample_description: Protocols: Fusarium conidia were grown and cultivated in Erlenmeyer flasks that contain liquid complete medium as 25-40% of the total volume of the flask for 3 days on a rotary shaker at 175 rpm, at 28°C. The mycelium was then separated from the medium by filtration, washed up and stored at -80°C. Total RNA was prepared by grinding tissues in liquid nitrogen and total RNA was extracted by TRIzol reagent (TRIzol Plus RNA Purification Kit, Ambion) and processed following the protocol provided by manufacturer. To remove DNA within extraction and purification procedures, total RNA was treated with DNase (Qiagen), then total RNA was quantified and visualized on a Bioanalyzer (Agilent). Library preparation and RNAseq were carried out as described in the Illumina TruSeq RNA Sample Preparation v2 Guide, the Illumina HiSeq 1000 System User Guide (Illumina, Inc., San Diego, CA, USA), and the KAPA Library Quantification Kit - Illumina/ABI Prism User Guide (Kapa Biosystems, Inc., Woburn, MA, USA). In brief, 500 ng of total RNA was used for purifying the poly-A containing mRNA molecules using poly-dT oligo-attached magnetic beads. Following purification, the mRNA was fragmented to an average insert size of 200-400 bases using divalent cations under elevated temperature (94°C for 4 minutes). The cleaved RNA fragments were copied into first strand cDNA using reverse transcriptase and random primers, followed by second strand cDNA synthesis using DNA Polymerase I and RNase H. The resulting cDNA fragments subsequently went through an end repair process, the addition of a single ‘A’ base, the ligation of the adapters, and a purification step. Finally the cDNA libraries were created by PCR enrichment. The libraries were quantified using the KAPA SYBR FAST ABI Prism Library Quantification Kit. Equimolar amounts of each library were used for cluster generation on the cBot (TruSeq PE Cluster Kit v3)

study_title: RNA-seq of Fusarium graminearum under predation by the springtail Folsomia candida against untreated controls
experiment_title: NextSeq 500 paired end sequencing: RNA-seq of Fusarium graminearum under predation by the springtail Folsomia candida against untreated controls
sample_description: Protocols: Mycelium was harvested and springtails were removed. Whole mycelium was used to extract the RNA. 5,000 fungal spores in 5 µL water were inoculated onto three rice kernels autoclaved with 200 µl demineralized water in 15 ml Falcon tubes and incubated at 15°C in dark for 7-8 days 20 mg (around 200 individual animal) of springtail Folsomia candida starved for two days were placed into mycelia and the incubated at 15°C in dark. Controls were incubated under the same conditions without animals. Each group consisted of 4 replicates. Suspension of mycelia in 400 µl of RNA extraction solution [95% deionized formamide, 18 mM EDTA, 0.025% SDS, and 1% 2-mercaptoethanol] was disrupted by shaking with zirconia beads (2.0 mm diameter, Carl Roth, Karlsruhe, Germany) in reciprocal mill MM 200 (Retsch, Haan, Germany) for 2 min at maximum power, followed by incubation at 95°C for 7 min. Cells debris was removed by centrifugation at 16,000x g for 5 min at room temperature. The supernatant was transferred into RNA precipitation mixture consisting of 800 µl of isobutanol, 400 µl of 5 M guanidine thiocyanate and 5 µl of linear polyacrylamide used as co-precipitant (Co-Precipitant Pink, Bioline, London, UK). The mixture was centrifuged at 16,000x g for 5 min at room temperature and the pellet was washed with 75% ethanol, dried and dissolved in RNAase-free water. Strand-specific cDNA libraries were prepared using Illumina’s TruSeq stranded mRNA kit (75 bp paired-end).
description: NextSeq 500 paired end sequencing: RNA-seq of Fusarium graminearum under predation by the springtail Folsomia candida against untreated controls

study_title: Transcriptome-based comparison of the infection response in maize silks between Fusarium graminearum and Ustilago maydis
experiment_title: Illumina HiSeq 1000 paired end sequencing: Transcriptome-based comparison of the infection response in maize silks between Fusarium graminearum and Ustilago maydis
sample_description: Protocols: Fusarium conidia were grown and cultivated in Erlenmeyer flasks that contain liquid complete medium as 25-40% of the total volume of the flask for 3 days on a rotary shaker at 175 rpm, at 28°C. The mycelium was then separated from the medium by filtration, washed up and stored at -80°C. Total RNA was prepared by grinding tissues in liquid nitrogen and total RNA was extracted by TRIzol reagent (TRIzol Plus RNA Purification Kit, Ambion) and processed following the protocol provided by manufacturer. To remove DNA within extraction and purification procedures, total RNA was treated with DNase (Qiagen), then total RNA was quantified and visualized on a Bioanalyzer (Agilent). Library preparation and RNAseq were carried out as described in the Illumina TruSeq RNA Sample Preparation v2 Guide, the Illumina HiSeq 1000 System User Guide (Illumina, Inc., San Diego, CA, USA), and the KAPA Library Quantification Kit - Illumina/ABI Prism User Guide (Kapa Biosystems, Inc., Woburn, MA, USA). In brief, 500 ng of total RNA was used for purifying the poly-A containing mRNA molecules using poly-dT oligo-attached magnetic beads. Following purification, the mRNA was fragmented to an average insert size of 200-400 bases using divalent cations under elevated temperature (94°C for 4 minutes). The cleaved RNA fragments were copied into first strand cDNA using reverse transcriptase and random primers, followed by second strand cDNA synthesis using DNA Polymerase I and RNase H. The resulting cDNA fragments subsequently went through an end repair process, the addition of a single ‘A’ base, the ligation of the adapters, and a purification step. Finally the cDNA libraries were created by PCR enrichment. The libraries were quantified using the KAPA SYBR FAST ABI Prism Library Quantification Kit. Equimolar amounts of each library were used for cluster generation on the cBot (TruSeq PE Cluster Kit v3)

study_title: RNA-seq of Fusarium graminearum under predation by the springtail Folsomia candida against untreated controls
experiment_title: NextSeq 500 paired end sequencing: RNA-seq of Fusarium graminearum under predation by the springtail Folsomia candida against untreated controls
sample_description: Protocols: Mycelium was harvested and springtails were removed. Whole mycelium was used to extract the RNA. 5,000 fungal spores in 5 µL water were inoculated onto three rice kernels autoclaved with 200 µl demineralized water in 15 ml Falcon tubes and incubated at 15°C in dark for 7-8 days 20 mg (around 200 individual animal) of springtail Folsomia candida starved for two days were placed into mycelia and the incubated at 15°C in dark. Controls were incubated under the same conditions without animals. Each group consisted of 4 replicates. Suspension of mycelia in 400 µl of RNA extraction solution [95% deionized formamide, 18 mM EDTA, 0.025% SDS, and 1% 2-mercaptoethanol] was disrupted by shaking with zirconia beads (2.0 mm diameter, Carl Roth, Karlsruhe, Germany) in reciprocal mill MM 200 (Retsch, Haan, Germany) for 2 min at maximum power, followed by incubation at 95°C for 7 min. Cells debris was removed by centrifugation at 16,000x g for 5 min at room temperature. The supernatant was transferred into RNA precipitation mixture consisting of 800 µl of isobutanol, 400 µl of 5 M guanidine thiocyanate and 5 µl of linear polyacrylamide used as co-precipitant (Co-Precipitant Pink, Bioline, London, UK). The mixture was centrifuged at 16,000x g for 5 min at room temperature and the pellet was washed with 75% ethanol, dried and dissolved in RNAase-free water. Strand-specific cDNA libraries were prepared using Illumina’s TruSeq stranded mRNA kit (75 bp paired-end).
